title: Early contact with Harold Dejan and meeting him in 1956
summary: He knew Dejan's family through childhood friends but first met him in 1956 while touring with rhythm and blues bands.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And did Harold Deshawn live in that neighborhood?
Harold lived in the Southern Water, I'd say yeah. Somewhere around the Neck or St. Anthony or somewhere when he was a younger man.
I was wondering if you had contact with him as a kid. I didn't know.

I had contact with him as a kid but didn't know it. Because his sister and my mother were great friends and his sister ran a cleaning shop on Saint Bernard Street Street near Claybond. And when I would come home from school I would go to his sister's house to stay until my mother and father came home from work, you know, in those early days. He had came, he must have visited his sister at one time or another, but I didn't know because his nephew was named Gene Jackson. And Gene Jackson was my very best friend in the grammar school and so forth. I went to his house every evening to play for a while before going home knowing that my mother and father would get home from work.
So you all intersected at that point? But we didn't know. Years later you all went.
Oh many years later. 1950, oh gee, 1956.
That was the first time you'd worked with Harold?

That's the first time I met him in 1956. I heard about him, seen him on the street and so forth. But at that time I was traveling on the road with different road bands, rhythm and blues bands at the time. Sherilyn Lee, Lil Walter, Jimmy Reed. We used to work out of a local office here in New Orleans, Stovall, Percy Stovall was involved in booking bands and so forth. And so naturally we went out on gigs, you know, from Shaw, a booking agency out of New York. Milt Shaw was the guy who was doing all the big time R&B booking at the time. So we, that's what I was doing. And then my father, one day, this is 1960, but I would say.
